metadata.environment: lab/misconfigured (moto emulated account, not a live AWS account)
metadata.severity_disclaimer: Severity is this project's internal prioritisation model. It is not a CVSS score, an AWS risk rating, or a formal industry classification.

findings.title: IAM policy grants unrestricted actions on all resources
findings.description: The inline policy 'lab-full-admin' attached to user 'lab-admin-console-nomfa' contains an Allow statement for Action "*" on all resources. The statement grants every action against every resource in the account. This reports the shape of the policy document; it does not evaluate service control policies, permissions boundaries, or session policies that may constrain the principal in practice.
findings.remediation: Replace the wildcard statement with the specific actions the workload calls, scoped to specific resource ARNs. Derive the action list from CloudTrail or IAM Access Analyzer policy generation rather than guessing.
findings.rationale: The statement grants every action against every resource, including the IAM actions needed to grant further access and the CloudTrail actions needed to stop recording it. Compromise of any principal holding it is equivalent to compromise of the account.

compliance.framework: CIS Amazon Web Services Foundations Benchmark v3.0.0
compliance.control_title: Ensure IAM policies that allow full "*:*" administrative privileges are not attached

findings.title: Bucket ACL grants public access
findings.description: The ACL on bucket 'lab-public-assets' grants READ to the global group(s) AllUsers. IgnorePublicAcls is not enabled, so the grants are effective.
findings.remediation: Remove the global-group grants from the bucket ACL, then enable Block Public Access so the grant cannot be reintroduced.
findings.rationale: AllUsers means anonymous callers on the internet. AuthenticatedUsers is commonly misread as 'my account' but means any AWS account holder, so both grants place the bucket outside the account's trust boundary.

findings.title: Bucket policy grants access to a public principal
findings.description: The bucket policy on 'lab-public-assets' contains an Allow statement with an anonymous principal. The statements grant access to anonymous callers without any condition.
findings.remediation: Scope the Principal to specific account or role ARNs. If the bucket must serve public content, front it with CloudFront and an origin access control rather than a public bucket policy.
findings.rationale: An anonymous Allow in the resource policy grants access without any authentication, independently of IAM. Conditions can narrow it, but they have to be read: an aws:SourceIp condition constrains access while an aws:SecureTransport condition does not.

findings.title: CloudTrail trail exists but is not currently logging
findings.description: Trail 'lab-single-region-trail' is configured but GetTrailStatus reports that logging is stopped. It appears correctly configured in any configuration-only review while recording nothing.
findings.remediation: Start logging on the trail and investigate why it stopped. For delivery errors, check the destination bucket policy, the bucket's existence, and the KMS key policy if the trail is encrypted.
findings.rationale: A configured trail is not the same as an operating one. A stopped trail or a failing delivery leaves the same gap as having no trail at all, while still appearing correctly configured in every configuration-only review.

findings.title: Console-enabled IAM user lacks MFA
findings.description: IAM user 'lab-admin-console-nomfa' has a console login profile but no MFA device is registered, so interactive sign-in is protected by a password alone.
findings.remediation: Register a virtual or hardware MFA device for the user, or delete the login profile if the identity only needs programmatic access.
findings.rationale: Console sign-in for this user depends on a password alone, so a single credential disclosure -- phishing, reuse, or a leaked password store -- is sufficient to obtain an interactive session in the account.

findings.title: Active IAM access key exceeds maximum age
findings.description: Access key AKIA…GQIJ for user 'lab-svc-stale-keys' is 400 days old, above the configured rotation threshold of 90 days and above the escalation threshold of 180 days. Key age is credential metadata; it does not by itself indicate that the key has been used or compromised.
findings.remediation: Create a replacement key, migrate dependent workloads, then deactivate and delete the superseded key. Prefer IAM roles or IAM Identity Center over long-lived user keys where the workload allows it.
findings.rationale: A long-lived static credential accumulates exposure: every backup, CI log, laptop, and container image it was ever copied into remains a live path into the account until the key is rotated.

findings.title: IAM policy grants service-wide permissions on all resources
findings.description: The managed policy 'lab-broad-service-access' attached to group 'lab-developers' allows service-wide wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*) on all resources. Whether that is excessive depends on the workload; the scanner reports the policy shape, not an effective-permissions verdict.
findings.remediation: Enumerate the actions the workload calls and replace the wildcard, scoping Resource to specific ARNs where the service supports it.
findings.rationale: Service-wide wildcards grant the destructive and permission-changing actions of a service alongside the read actions a workload actually needs -- s3:* includes s3:DeleteBucket and s3:PutBucketPolicy. Whether that is excessive depends on the workload, which is why this is reported for review rather than as an outright administrative grant.

findings.title: No multi-region CloudTrail trail configured
findings.description: All 1 configured trail(s) are single-region, so activity in any other region is not captured. Regions an organisation does not use are exactly where unmonitored activity tends to occur.
findings.remediation: Convert an existing trail to multi-region (IsMultiRegionTrail with IncludeGlobalServiceEvents), or create a dedicated multi-region trail.
findings.rationale: Activity in unmonitored regions is not recorded. Attackers routinely operate in regions an organisation does not use precisely because logging and detection are usually configured only where workloads run.

findings.title: CloudTrail log file validation is disabled
findings.description: Log file validation is disabled for trail 'lab-single-region-trail', so CloudTrail is not producing the signed digest files needed to prove that delivered logs have not been modified or deleted.
findings.remediation: Enable log file validation on the trail (update-trail --enable-log-file-validation).
findings.rationale: Without the signed digest files that validation produces, a deleted or modified log file cannot be distinguished from one that never existed, which removes the log's value as incident evidence.

findings.title: Dormant IAM access key remains active
findings.description: Active access key AKIA…GQIJ for user 'lab-svc-stale-keys' has never been used in 400 days since creation (GetAccessKeyLastUsed reports no last-used date), at or beyond the 45-day dormancy threshold. An unused credential retains the full permissions of its user while producing no activity that would make its misuse noticeable.
findings.remediation: Delete the key. If the workload may still need it, deactivate it first and delete it once a full billing cycle passes with no access failures.
findings.rationale: A credential nobody uses is a credential nobody is watching. Dormant keys carry the full permissions of their user while producing no signal that would make their misuse noticeable, and an Inactive key can be re-enabled by anyone who can call UpdateAccessKey.

findings.title: S3 Public Access Block is not fully enabled
findings.description: Bucket 'lab-latent-acl' has Public Access Block settings disabled: BlockPublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, RestrictPublicBuckets. This does not by itself mean the bucket is public; it means a public ACL or bucket policy would not be blocked if one were applied.
findings.remediation: Enable all four Block Public Access settings on the bucket, and enable the account-level block, unless the bucket is intentionally serving public content.
findings.rationale: Block Public Access is the backstop that makes a public ACL or bucket policy non-effective even when one is applied by mistake. With it off, a single careless PutBucketAcl call is enough to expose the bucket.

findings.title: Bucket policy grants access to a public principal
findings.description: The bucket policy on 'lab-partner-share' contains an Allow statement with an anonymous principal. Every public statement carries a narrowing condition (aws:sourceip), so access may be limited to a specific network or organisation. The condition needs manual review; a scanner cannot tell whether the named range is trusted.
findings.remediation: Scope the Principal to specific account or role ARNs. If the bucket must serve public content, front it with CloudFront and an origin access control rather than a public bucket policy.
findings.rationale: An anonymous Allow in the resource policy grants access without any authentication, independently of IAM. Conditions can narrow it, but they have to be read: an aws:SourceIp condition constrains access while an aws:SecureTransport condition does not.

findings.title: No explicit bucket-level encryption configuration observed
findings.description: GetBucketEncryption returned no bucket-level default encryption configuration for 'lab-public-assets'. Amazon S3 has applied SSE-S3 to new objects by default since January 2023, so this records the absence of an explicit, auditable configuration rather than asserting that stored objects are unencrypted.
findings.remediation: Set an explicit default encryption configuration (SSE-S3, or SSE-KMS with a customer-managed key where key-level access control or auditing is required).
findings.rationale: S3 has applied SSE-S3 to new objects by default since January 2023, so this is an evidence and enforcement gap rather than plaintext storage: there is no configuration to audit, no way to require SSE-KMS, and no key policy boundary around the data.

findings.title: IAM user without MFA (no console access configured)
findings.description: IAM user 'lab-svc-rotating' has no console login profile and no MFA device. There is no interactive sign-in path to protect, so this is recorded for inventory completeness rather than as an authentication weakness.
findings.remediation: No MFA action is required while the identity remains programmatic-only. Re-evaluate if console access is enabled.
findings.rationale: There is no interactive sign-in path to protect, so this is not a console authentication weakness. It is recorded so the inventory of MFA-less identities is complete and so the finding reappears at a higher tier if a login profile is added later.
